children.game_version: A rhythmic stick-tapping game performed in a circle where children match their strikes to a steady drumbeat.

seniors.counts: Count in steady 4/4 time without acceleration.
seniors.seated_version: Perform the stick-striking patterns while seated in a chair, keeping upper body movements moderate.
seniors.standing_version: Stand in place without traveling in a circle, practicing stick strikes at a reduced, steady tempo.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduced tempo with limited range of motion for deep bends and leaps.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Wielding two-foot long sticks, striking stick against stick in attack and defense
movement_profile.footwork: Special steps and footwork borrowed directly from Kalarippayattu
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Circular formation where the circle expands and contracts as the dance progresses
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Body extension and deep bending required in performance
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Includes leaps, turns, and deep bends
movement_profile.posture: Body postures and deep bends taken directly from Kalarippayattu training

signature_moves.description: Dancers move in an expanding and contracting circle while striking two-foot sticks together.
signature_moves.name: Stick Striking Circle

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Begins with a slow tempo that gradually increases

music_profile.sound_description: The music features driving percussion from a small Chenda drum and small cymbals, accompanied by group singing. The sound begins at a slow, measured pace and progressively increases in pitch and tempo, driving the dancers toward an energetic climax.

basic_steps: Circular formation step keeping rhythm with special steps
Striking two-foot-long sticks in attack and defense patterns
teaching.formation: Circular formation of 10 to 20 dancers (12 to 16 in Lakshadweep)
teaching.level_notes: Requires physical stamina, deep bends, and coordination derived from martial art conditioning.
teaching.rhythm: Begins with a slow tempo that gradually increases in speed and pitch toward a climax
